what: Veeva Systems makes software for pharmaceutical and biotech companies: systems for running clinical trials, managing regulatory submissions, controlling quality, and managing relationships with doctors.
customers: Pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies of all sizes, plus contract research organisations.
money: clinical trial, regulatory and quality management software
CRM and data for sales and marketing to doctors
moat: Software validated for regulated pharmaceutical processes, where switching means revalidating systems with regulators, and an industry-specific design no general software vendor matches.
risks: It is tied to one industry, so a pharmaceutical spending downturn hits everything
It is replacing Salesforce underneath its commercial products, a large migration
Biotech funding weakness reduces spending by smaller customers
The shares trade at a high multiple of earnings
opportunities: Revenue grew about 16% last year with a 29% operating margin
Cash of about $7 billion against almost no debt
Its own data products compete with established pharmaceutical data vendors
watch: Customer migrations to its own CRM platform, and subscription revenue growth.
